label: late-episode drop deepened by a2 lean (policy, last choice)
terms: (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * choice ;; (phase == D1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * choice ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) ;; (phase == D1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * (table(prev_state,{1:1,2:-1})*table(prev_reward,{1:1,0:-1})) ;; (phase == D1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * (table(prev_state,{1:1,2:-1})*table(prev_reward,{1:1,0:-1})) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * choice * (prev_reward==1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/10.) * value
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 22 sits near +1 (saturated) and falls late in the episode, mostly at GO (decile-10 mean 0.43) and less at D1; D2 stays near 1. Timing alone gives R^2 0.86. Beyond timing, what sets the size of the late drop is how much the agent leans to a2. All terms are scaled by exp((ep_trial-99)/10), so they only matter in the last ~20 trials. The drop is deeper when the policy logit favours a2 (choice < 0, at D1 and GO, and more so after a rewarded trial) and when the previous choice was a2 (strongest at D1), with small terms for the last trial state x reward and for value at GO. Late a2 runs with common-rewarded S2 push GO to about -0.1; late a1 trials stay high. Within-decile timing alone adds only 0.03. Additive tables of the profile cues reach only 0.18 (all ceiling) because they ignore the late-episode interaction. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.46, test 0.39. Large errors remain between episodes: some late a2 runs stay at 0.5-0.7 while others reach ~0, and these terms do not capture that. No future variables are used (choice and value are model outputs at that step).
